name: Sedang
catalog_quote: PHONOLOGICAL WORDS. Phonological words in Sedang are either mono- or bisyllabic. Monosyllabic words consist of one (usually) stressed "main syllable". Bisyllabic words consist of a preliminary unstressed "presyllable" and a (following) stressed main syllable.

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-strict, stress on the final = main syllable of a maximally bisyllabic presyllable+main-syllable word) rests on a verbatim, page-confirmed statement in the standard reference grammar (Smith 1979 PL B-50, section 4.1 p. 20), which we hold as full PDF and text; the same book repeats the pattern at 4.4 (p. 46) and 12.3 (p. 149), and notes monosyllabic function words are often unstressed in context (p. 21), none of which conflicts with the coding. No better or instrumental source exists per Glottolog and Crossref; the only newer work is a 2014 Brill handbook sketch by the same author with Sidwell (paywalled), unlikely to change anything. The record's top-level quote/cite/grade fields are blank while the verbatim primary quotation sits in 'sources'/'dq', so the only action suggested is to populate the evidence grade as primary-source-verified; no recode.
